12.3: Sohila: Raag Gauri Deepaki, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. In the house where (God's) praise is spoken and the Creator is reflected upon, in that house sing the Sohila and remember the Creator. Sing the Sohila of my Fearless Lord. I am a sacrifice to the Sohila by which there is peace for ever. Day after day all beings are cared for; the Giver will watch over (each one). (O soul,) you cannot set a value on his giving; what measure can be taken of that Giver? The year and the day (of my wedding) have been written; gather, (friends,) and pour the oil (of the wedding rite). Give me your blessings, friends, so that I may be united with my Master. To every house this same summons comes; these calls go out every day. Let us remember the One who sends the call; O Nanak, those days are coming (for us too). ॥4॥
Sohila is a song of joy and praise, like the wedding songs sung on the nights before a marriage. Five shabads stand under this name, recited at night before sleep.

Stanzas 3 and 4 draw on the wedding rites: the year and the day of the wedding (saaha) are fixed in writing, the invitation (paahucha) goes to the houses of kin, and the bride's friends gather to pour the oil and give their blessings. Here the wedding is death, when the soul-bride goes to her Husband Lord.
12.4: Raag Asa, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). Six are the schools, six (their) teachers, and six (their) teachings; but the Guru of these teachers is the One (God), whose guises are many. O brother, the house (the school) in which the Creator is praised: hold fast to that house; in it lies your greatness. Visas, chasas, gharis, pahars, lunar days and weekdays (together) make up the month; the sun is one and the seasons many; (in the same way,) O Nanak, the Creator has so many guises. ॥2॥

The six houses are the six schools (darshanas) of Indian philosophy: Nyaya, Vaisheshika, Sankhya, Yoga, Mimamsa and Vedanta; the six teachers are their founders: Gautama, Kanada, Kapila, Patanjali, Jaimini and Vyasa.

The units of time: a visa is the time of fifteen blinks of the eye, fifteen visas make a chasa; a ghari is about twenty-four minutes and a pahar about three hours; the lunar days (thitis) are the dates of the moon's calendar.
13.1: Raag Dhanasari, by the First Guru (Guru Nanak Dev Ji). The sky is the platter; the sun and the moon are its lamps, and the clusters of stars are like pearls; the sandal-scented breeze from the Malaya hills is the incense, the wind waves the fly-whisk, and all the plant life blossoms for the Light (that is God). What a wondrous aarti this is! O Destroyer of the round of births, this is your aarti: the unstruck sound resounds as its drums. Thousands are your eyes, yet you have no eye; thousands are your forms, yet not one form is yours; thousands are your spotless feet, yet you have not one foot; you are without a nose, yet thousands are your noses: these wonders of yours have enchanted me. Within all is the light, and that light is he. By his radiance there is light within all. Through the Guru's teaching this light becomes manifest. Whatever pleases him, that becomes the aarti. My mind is lured by the nectar of the Lord's lotus feet; night and day I thirst for it. Give Nanak, the rain-bird, the water of your grace, by which he may abide in your Name. ॥4॥

Aarti is the worship in which a platter of lamps, incense and flowers is waved before an image; in this shabad all of nature performs the Creator's aarti. Malaanalo (malaya + anila, wind) is the fragrant breeze from the sandalwood hills of Malaya in the south of India; the fly-whisk (chaur) is waved over one who is revered.
The Anhad (anāhata, unstruck) Shabad is the sound made by no striking: the divine music that sounds unbroken through all creation.
The saaring (papiha, the rain-bird) is said to drink only drops of rain, and to keep calling out for them.
13.2: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The city (of the body) is filled to the brim with lust and anger; meeting the Saadh (the Guru), these are smashed to pieces. By the writ of the past the Guru has been found, and loving absorption (liv) in the Lord is set like a jewel in the mind. Join your palms before the Saadh: this is a great merit. Lie stretched out before him in prostration: this is a great merit. The Saakats (those who have turned from God) have not known the taste of the Lord's sweet essence; within them is the thorn of Haumai (ego). The further they walk, the more it pricks and they suffer pain, and they bear the rod of Jamkaal (death) upon their heads. The Lord's servants remain merged in the Name of the Lord, Har Har; they have cut away the pain of birth and death in the world. They have found the imperishable, all-pervading Supreme God, and great is their glory across the lands and universes. We are poor and meek, God, and we are yours; save us, O Lord, save us: you are the greatest of the great. Servant Nanak's support and prop is the Naam; in the Lord's Name alone has peace been found. ॥4॥
The ਹੇ that ends every line is not an address (O) but an old form of ਹੈ, is: ਖੰਡਾ ਹੇ, has been broken; ਪੁਨੁ ਵਡਾ ਹੇ, is a great merit.
13.3: Raag Gauri Poorbi, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I make one request, my friends; listen: this is the time to serve the Sants. Earn the Lord's profit here before you depart, and your dwelling hereafter will be at ease. Day and night, the span of life wears away. O mind, meet the Guru and set your affairs right. This world is steeped in vice and caught in doubt; the Brahm Giani (one who knows God) has crossed over it. Whom (God) awakens and gives this sweet essence to drink, that one has come to know the story of the Indescribable. Buy the very thing you came for; through the Guru, the Lord comes to dwell within the mind. In your own home within, in the peace of Sahaj, you will find (his) mansion, and there will be no more round (of birth and death). O Knower of hearts, all-pervading Being, Creator, fulfil the longing of my mind. Servant Nanak begs for this one joy: make me the dust of the Sants' feet. ॥4॥
